translation:
Shennong Bencao Jing

Postscript to the Revised Edition

3. Cases where the citation source, the Zhenglei Bencao, contains omissions and misplacements:

4. "Bai [Huangbai bark] is the main treatment for sudden heat, eliminates water-qi, and promotes urination." Citation based on the Zhenglei Bencao Gangmu, juan 19.

1. The Tang Bencao removed twenty species, among them Guhuo, Bieli, Shizhang-chang-luan, Qiaogen, Qucao, and Huaimu — six species in total. Sun's edition restored Guhuo, Bieli, Qucao, and Huaimu to the upper-class herbal section, and added Qiaogen to the lower-class section, but inadvertently omitted the entry "Shi xia chang luan." See Zhenglei Bencao, juan 30.

2. The entry for White Kaolin (Bai Shizhi) states it uses the cormorant as a messenger, is incompatible with pine resin, and fears Scutellaria. In the Zhenglei Bencao's section on drug interactions following the Red Kaolin (Huang Shizhi) entry, the entire White Kaolin entry was dropped. See Zhenglei Bencao, juan 30.

3. The entry for longan (Longyan) cites a phrase from the Mingyi Bielu concerning pine moss (Songluo). The eight characters "on pine trees, dried in the shade during the fifth month" were mistakenly placed under the longan entry's citation from the Zhanguo Ce, rather than under the pine moss entry's citation from the Mingyi Bielu. See Zhanguo Ce, commentary by Gao You, juan 10.

4. In the entry for balloon-flower root (Jiegen), a passage from the Zhanguo Ce — the two sentences beginning "and going to the shaded side of Mount Liangfu, one unloads the cart" — was mistakenly placed after the phrase "now seeking Chaihu," rather than in its correct position.

5. The entry for Huaimu mistakenly incorporates the annotation belonging to the Zhansi entry, which reads: "The Mingyi says: another name is tan, grows on Mount Tai, harvested at no fixed season." This was incorrectly attributed as a note for Huaimu. See Zhenglei Bencao, juan 30.

6. The annotation for foxtail millet (Sumi) originally cited the Bielu as the source of the addition, but was mistakenly changed to cite Wu Pu. See Zhenglei Bencao, juan 25.

7. The annotation for broomcorn millet (Shumi) originally cited the Bielu as the source of the addition, but was mistakenly changed to cite Wu Pu. See Zhenglei Bencao, juan 25.

8. The entry for false perilla (Jiasu) cites a Tang Bencao annotation, but it was mistakenly attributed to Tao Hongjing's commentary. See Zhenglei Bencao, juan 28.

"One name: (jia) pepper."

"In the sixth month (the fruit grows large and ripens); like a plum and can be eaten."

Editorial Notes

Li Shizhen's Bencao Gangmu, citing Wu Pu's Bencao, writes "Bai (white)" as the character.

"Chong (worm/insect)" was mistakenly written as "huan (affliction)"; corrected according to the Zhenglei [Bencao].

"Ji (and/reaching)" was mistakenly written as "yu (withered)"; corrected according to the Yulan [imperial encyclopedia].

"Ye (leaf)" was mistakenly written as "yao (medicinal herb)"; corrected according to the annotation by Guo Pu in the Erya as cited in the Yulan.

"Rou (flesh/internal)" was mistakenly written as "nei (inner)"; corrected according to the Zhenglei [Bencao].

"Shu da zi (fruit ripening large)" written as "cheng shi da (fruit growing fully large)," corrected according to Ding Yan's ancient collation in the Jing Jie Hui Han, chapter fifteen, on plants, birds, beasts, insects and fish in the Mao Shi.

"Jia" was mistakenly written as "jia"; corrected according to the Zhenglei. Collation note.

The Zhou edition, citing Wu Pu's Bencao from the Yulan, writes "bi (clearing)" as "fu (returning/again)."

"Juan (curled)" was mistakenly written as "qu (cricket-like)"; corrected according to the Guangya Shuzheng.

廣志云（沙冠色赤大不過蠶）　又（八）月斷靈　食（蜜）為使　（藥）以蝸對參之　辛夷白薇　惡牡丹元石　消石（火）為使　甘草為使長（牡）蝱　（陽）起石　（柴）胡為使　細辛（昆）水　昆扁青茵陳蒿　女姜（姜）蕊（昆齒鹹）　惡貝母長（藤夷）

ORIGINAL TEXT:
Guangzhi says (all have beard-like color, red, larger than a silkworm); In the (ninth) month the Ling is cut; Food (honey) is used as envoy; (Medicines used paired with Shen); Xinyi white; Adverse to: mudanpi (Mu Meng, Yuan Shi), Xiao Shi (said) is used as envoy; Gancao used as envoy, grows (mu) horsefly; (Tang) Qishi; (Zihu) used as envoy; Xixin; Kun Bianqing Yinchen; Female ginger essence (governs Kun Meng salty); Adverse to Beimu, grows (without Yi).

CORRECTED TEXT:
Guangzhi says (sand-crown color red, not larger than a silkworm); In the (eighth) month the Ling is cut; Food (honey) is used as envoy; (Medicine) paired with snail opposing Shen; Xinyi, Baiwei; Adverse to mudanpi Yuan Shi; Xiao Shi (fire) used as envoy; Gancao used as envoy, grows (mu) horsefly; (Yang) Qishi; (Chai) Hu used as envoy; Xixin (Kun) water; Kun Bianqing Yinchen Hao; Female ginger (ginger) essence (Kun tooth salty); Adverse to Beimu, grows (Teng Yi).

TEXTUAL NOTES:
Based on the original text of Guangzhi there are omissions and errors; corrected using citations in Yulan referencing Guangzhi.
"Eight" was mistakenly written as "nine"; corrected using Guangzhi annotations citing Mao Shi.
"Mi (honey)" was mistakenly written as "mi (close)"; corrected using Yulan citing Sang Puyu.
"Yao (medicine)" was mistakenly written as another form; corrected using Zhenglei citing Tang Shenwei's notes.
Below "bai" the character "wei" is missing; corrected using Zhenglei.
Below "dan" two extra characters "Mu Meng" appear; corrected using Zhenglei.
Below "shi" the character "fire" appears extra; corrected using Zhenglei.
"Mu (mother)" should be "mu (male)"; corrected using Zhenglei.
"Yang" was mistakenly written as "Tang"; corrected using Zhenglei.
"Chai" was mistakenly written as "Zi"; corrected using Zhenglei.
Below "xin" the character "kun" is missing; corrected using Zhenglei.
Below "shu" the character "hao" is missing; corrected using Zhenglei.
The phrasing does not match the Zhenglei original text.
"Wu Yi" should be "Teng Yi"; corrected using Zhenglei.
